title: Plans & the future
goal: Talk about plans, intentions and hopes, and use the future tense with به.
intro:
Pashtuns are careful about the future: almost every plan comes with **انشاالله** 'God willing'. Grammatically, the future is easy once you know the perfective (unit 10): just add the little particle **به** (ba).

In this unit you'll learn to talk about next week, next year and your dreams (ارمان), to say what you *want to* and *intend to* do, and how to use 'maybe' and 'definitely'.

vocab.note: Unstressed; usually in second position. Also marks 'would' / habitual past.
m. پلان مې دی چې … 'my plan is to …'.
f. اراده لرم چې … 'I intend to …'.
m. Also 'regret' — a very Pashto word, common in poetry.
Often with the subjunctive: شايد راشي 'he may come'.
f. بله. بل کال 'next year', بله اوونۍ 'next week'.
m. چکر وهل 'to go on an outing'.
m. انتظار کول 'to wait'; ستا انتظار کوم 'I'm waiting for you'.
m. ګډون کول 'to take part, attend'.

grammar.title: The future: به + verb
grammar.body:
The future is the particle **به** (ba) + the **present** form of the verb. Like the clitics, به is unstressed and comes **after the first word or phrase** of the sentence: زه **به** راشم, سبا **به** راشم.

Which present form? The aspect tells you what kind of future:
• **به + perfective** (the usual choice): a single, complete future event. سبا به ورته زنګ **ووهم** 'I'll call him tomorrow'. نامه به **وليکم** 'I'll write the letter'.
• **به + imperfective**: an ongoing or repeated future action. هره ورځ به درته زنګ **وهم** 'I'll call you every day'. ستا انتظار به **کوم** 'I'll be waiting for you'.

'Will be' is **به … وي** (or به يم / به يې … for 1st and 2nd person): سبا به په کور کې يم 'I'll be at home tomorrow'.

Negative: نه goes before the verb — after the و- prefix in simple perfectives: به **و**نه خورم 'I won't eat'; به لاړ **نه** شم 'I won't go'.

grammar.title: Intentions: want to, plan to, try to
grammar.body:
Most 'intention' verbs are followed by **چې** + the **subjunctive** (the perfective present without به):

**غواړم چې …** 'I want to …': غواړم چې پښتو زده کړم
**اراده لرم چې …** 'I intend to …'
**پلان مې دی چې …** 'my plan is to …'
**کوښښ کوم چې …** 'I'm trying to …'
**ارمان مې دی چې …** 'my dream is to …'
**شايد** 'maybe' + subjunctive: شايد سبا راشم 'I may come tomorrow'.

The subject of the چې-clause can differ from the main subject: غواړم چې **ته** راشې 'I want **you** to come' (lit. I want that you come).

dialogue.title: Planning a picnic
dialogue.setting: It's March. Three friends — Ajmal, Rahim and Karim — plan a Nowruz outing to Paghman, near Kabul.

lines.en: My plan is for us to go on a picnic to Paghman.

lines.en: Great idea! The weather will be nice there.

lines.en: Early in the morning, at seven. I'll bring the car.

lines.en: I might be a bit late, because I'm going to the office in the morning.

lines.speaker: Rahim

lines.roman: mushkíl nə́shta, stā intizā́r ba kawú. xo hatmán rā́sha!
lines.en: No problem, we'll wait for you. But be sure to come!

culture: **Nowruz** (نوروز، د نوي کال ورځ, 21 March) is a major holiday in Afghanistan: families go on picnics (ميله) to gardens and hillsides like Paghman and Istalif, eat هفت مېوه (a dish of seven dried fruits) and celebrate the start of spring; in Pakistan it is less widely observed. Whatever the plan, you'll hear انشاالله — said sincerely, not as a polite 'no'. Pashtun men often speak of their **ارمان** — the dream of building a house, seeing their children educated, or returning home from abroad — and ارمان is one of the most frequent words in Pashto songs.

lessons.title: What are you doing tomorrow?

tip.title: The future: به + verb
tip.body:
- Put **به** after the first word or phrase, then the verb: سبا **به** راشم 'I'll come tomorrow'.
- For one event use the perfective: راشم، لاړ شم، وکړم.
- 'Will be': به + يم / يې / وي: سبا به په کور کې **يم**.
- بل 'next' agrees: **بل** کال، **بله** اوونۍ.

lessons.title: Plans and dreams

tip.title: Want to, plan to, try to
tip.body:
- These all take **چې** + the perfective, with a person ending and no به: غواړم **چې** زده **کړم**.
- **پلان مې دی چې** … · **اراده لرم چې** … · **کوښښ کوم چې** … · **ارمان مې دی چې** ….
- **شايد** 'maybe' works the same: شايد ناوخته **شم**.
- 'I want **you** to come': غواړم چې ته راش**ې**.
